user_prompt: What is the effect of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS, including deep TMS and theta-burst stimulation), compared with sham stimulation, on PTSD symptom severity in adults with post-traumatic stress disorder, measured as the change from baseline to the assessment immediately after treatment?  Effect measure: pool as a standardised mean difference (SMD, Hedges' g) using a random-effects model. SMD < 0 means a greater reduction in PTSD symptoms with active rTMS (favours rTMS).  Outcome: change in PTSD symptom severity from baseline to immediately after the course of treatment, on the trial's primary validated PTSD scale (for example the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale, the PTSD Checklist, or the Davidson Trauma Scale), extracted as the mean change, SD of change and number of participants per arm. - Use the intention-to-treat (all randomised, or all analysed in the trial's primary analysis) result. Accept the trial's own primary analysis (for example a mixed model, last observation carried forward, multiple imputation or "all randomised participants analysed") even if the method for missing data is not named in detail. Do not require an explicit statement of imputation. - If the paper reports baseline and post-treatment means and SDs per arm but not the change, calculate the mean change as post-treatment minus baseline for each arm. Estimate the SD of the change from the baseline and post-treatment SDs, assuming a correlation of 0.5 between the two measurements, and state that the change and its SD were derived. - If the paper reports the mean change and SD of change directly, use them. - If variability is reported as SE or SEM, convert to SD = SE × √n. Check table footnotes for whether "±" is SD or SE. - Use the assessment closest to the end of the treatment course (immediately after treatment). Do not use follow-up assessments weeks or months later. - Use the scale on which a higher score means worse PTSD; if a scale is oriented the other way, reverse its sign. - Use the number randomised or analysed in the primary analysis for each arm. If arm sizes are not stated in the text, use the sizes in the participant-flow diagram or the table of results. - Control: sham rTMS (a sham coil or sham stimulation). Exclude trials with no sham arm. - Multi-arm trials: include the active rTMS arm and the sham arm only; if there are two active arms, combine them into one group (sum participants) and use the sham group once. - Include only randomised sham-controlled trials in adults with PTSD. Exclude open-label and uncontrolled studies.  Do not pool depression, anxiety, quality of life, adverse events, dropouts, or any non-PTSD outcome.
